# pnpm-workspace

### 1. Create pnpm-workspace.yaml
Create a file called **pnpm-workspace.yaml** in the root of the project and put the following input and format it like so:

```yaml
packages:
- "backend"
- "frontend"
```

The purpose of this is to define which folder should be part of the workspace, this will allow for shared dependencies between packages to be installed efficiently. It will prevent unnecessary duplication of dependencies across subproject and enables cross-package linking within the workspace.
### 2. Add concurrently
This will allow us to run multiple terminal instances together and to switch easily between the different environments. Since this is in the root, we need to add the -w flag to tell pnpm that we want to install this dependency intentionally:

```bash
pnpm add -D concurrently -w
```

:::note Note:
This will create a node\_modules folder like pnpm install if it doesn't exist yet. If you don't know what the node\_modules folder is, its a directory where every dependency will be installed in.
:::
### 3. Create a file called .gitignore

In the root of your project, create a file called **.gitignore**. Then copy and paste the template from the example below into your **.gitignore** file:

[https://github.com/github/gitignore/blob/main/Node.gitignore](https://github.com/github/gitignore/blob/main/Node.gitignore)

Now also add the following line under the other ignores to exclude the `node_modules/` directory from entering the git space:

```plain
**/node_modules
```

This way when you commit code in the future the dependencies we don't want in the repository won't be committed.

# Prettier

### 1. Add prettier
To install prettier intentionally in the root, we need to add the -w flag to tell pnpm that we want to add the **prettier packages** to the `package.json` in the `root` directory of the workspace:

```bash
pnpm add -D prettier prettier-plugin-svelte prettier-plugin-tailwindcss -w
```

### 2. Create .prettierrc
Create a **.prettierrc** file in the `root` directory of your project, with the json from the example below. Then look at the values in your file, these are some default formatting settings we apply to our project. What's important is that we force our projects to use the method `LF` instead of `CLRF`

```json
{
	"useTabs": true,
	"tabWidth": 4,
	"endOfLine": "lf",
	"semi": false,
	"singleQuote": true,
	"trailingComma": "all",
	"printWidth": 150,
	"plugins": [
		"prettier-plugin-svelte",
		"prettier-plugin-tailwindcss"
	],
	"overrides": [
		{
			"files": "*.svelte",

		}
	]
}
```

Create a **.prettierignore** in the `root` directory of your project, with the text from the example below. These texts represent the files and folders you want prettier to ignore when formatting.

# Package Managers
